lucas_presales: Heads-up — CartersCorp asked for minimal POC evidence for BYOK/HSM and CAIQ questions today. They want: who holds keys, rotation policy, proof HSM prevents key export, and a tiny conductible test they can run during the trial. What can we give quickly?

imelda_security: We can produce a 1-page summary + a tiny test harness. Summary should state: TLS1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, envelope encryption using customer CMK, Redwood-managed KMS (default) or BYOK via customer KMS/HSM. Also include audit/logging and key usage events (CloudTrail/KMS logs).
\maya_sales: Need to be lightweight — customer security team only has 30 mins in the POC call. They asked for a reproducible command they can run and a sentence about exportability.

lucas_presales: OK. Proposed deliverables: 1) 1-page answers to the relevant CAIQ questions (encryption & key mgmt), 2) an automated smoke test (small script) that demonstrates envelope encrypt/decrypt using a provided CMK, 3) sample audit snippet showing a key usage event. Thoughts?

imelda_security: +1. Key points to state in CAIQ: keys are immutable in HSM (no export), we perform CMK rotation per-customer schedule (default 90d), and we store KMS audit logs for 13 months (configurable). Also include the legal note: Redwood cannot access plaintext when customer provides BYOK/HSM and policies are strict.

carter_cust: Quick Q — when you say "no export from HSM" what exact HSMs do you support? We run Azure and AWS and also evaluate on-prem Thales.

imelda_security: We support AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM for Private/Dedicated. For on-prem Thales, we have an adapter pack for our Private deployment (requires customer coordination). Key takeaway: HSM-backed CMKs are non-exportable by design; we describe the attestation model in the doc.

andre_sre: For the smoke test we can provide an AWS CLI example and a tiny wrapper that uses envelope encryption. Example command clients can run against a test key we create in their account (if BYOK) or our test CMK (if they want quick demo):

```
aws kms generate-data-key --key-id alias/RedwoodPOC --key-spec AES_256 --query CiphertextBlob --output text | base64 --decode > ciphertext.bin
# then decrypt
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --query Plaintext --output text | base64 --decode > plaintext.bin
```

andre_sre: Add note: for HSM-backed CMKs the CLI works the same; ciphertext never exposes raw key material and HSM prevents export.

maya_sales: Price question from procurement: does BYOK/HSM change cost during POC? We need a short sentence for the SOW.

\lucas_presales: Short answer for SOW: BYOK integration is included for Private/Dedicated; HSM connectors may incur an infra add-on (one-time integration + small monthly for HSM bridging). Put as "may add an integration fee and an ongoing HSM support add-on" — commercial will follow up with numbers after technical ok.

carter_cust: Can you provide the audit snippet you mentioned? We want to match to our vendor risk review template.

imelda_security: Will provide a redacted CloudTrail/KMS event showing a GenerateDataKey/Decrypt call with principal and request parameters. Example snippet (redacted) included in the one-pager. Also include the CAIQ mapping lines: "encryption at-rest: AES-256; in-transit: TLS1.2/1.3; KMS: customer-managed supported; HSM: non-exportable; key rotation: configurable (default 90d)."

lucas_presales: Action list: @imelda_security to produce 1-page CAIQ answer + redacted audit snippet; @andre_sre to create smoke test script and short README; @maya_sales to add the SOW sentence. I'll deliver to Carter by EOD. @carter_cust does that timeline work for you?

carter_cust: That works, thanks. Looking forward to the one-pager — will review in the POC call. :thumbsup:

redwood_deploybot: POC env provisioned: redwood-poc-carter-01 in us-east-1 (demo CMK alias/RedwoodPOC created, logging enabled).

lucas_presales: Great — I'll attach the one-pager and the script to the CAIQ reply. Keep the POC test to a single command for the call.

imelda_security: I'll mention compliance artifacts too (SOC2 cert pointer and encryption control mapping) so they can link during vendor review.

maya_sales: TY all — I'll draft the SOW line and loop legal if needed. :raised_hands:

carter_cust: Perfect, talk on the POC call.
